**Fieldbook 2.2.3 beta 2** (a beta)
### Changed - **File › Send Folders to iPhone or iPad…** (was Send Folders to iPhone…): Fieldbook for iPhone runs on the iPad too. - **Help Me Answer shows its points as they're written,** so the first ones appear in about a second with a cloud model. - **Updates no longer prepare the speech model again:** Fieldbook keeps its own copy of the model in its Application Support folder, so after an update the first transcription starts right away instead of taking about 15 seconds longer and writing about 1.5 GB to disk. The copy takes about 1.6 GB once an update has replaced the app's own. - **Fieldbook Help is easier to read:** each section in the sidebar has an icon and a line above it, and every topic was rewritten short and to the point: a plain line and a few bullets, with the rest under **Details** (search and Ask AI in Help still find it, and a search opens it).
### Fixed - **A link in your notes can be removed:** right-click a web or email address › **Remove Link** keeps it as plain text (**Make Link** turns it back). Before, it became a link again at once.

**Fieldbook 2.2.3 beta 1** (a beta)
### Added - **Live transcript while recording:** a draft of what's said, as it's said, in a **Live draft** column beside your notes: **You** and **Them**, a few seconds behind, the newest words in grey until they settle. It's made on this Mac with the same speech model, and nothing leaves the Mac. **Pause** stops it for a while; **Live** in the recording bar shows or hides it. After the call it stays until the full transcript, with each person's name, replaces it. Turn it off, or have it pause on battery, in **Settings › Transcription › Live transcript**. While it's on, earlier meetings wait to transcribe until the recording ends. - **Help Me Answer:** in a call, click **Help Me Answer** under the live draft, or press **Control-Option-H** from any app, for 3 to 5 points to say next about what was just asked, from the last couple of minutes of the call, the account's summary, your company's solutions, and, when the call is about licensing, the best passages of your licensing library (click one to open it). Only when you ask. It uses the **Quick tasks** model (Settings › AI › Models) for speed. Change the shortcut in **Settings › General › Shortcuts**. - **A model for quick tasks:** **Settings › AI › Models › Quick tasks** lets a cheaper model, such as Claude Haiku or Sonnet, do the matching and extracting (Discovery answers, Account Discovery, MEDDPICC's evidence from each meeting, which customers a meeting is about, the licensing match) while your summary model writes notes, summaries, briefs, and emails. It starts as **Same as summary model**. - **Field takeaways from training:** a training's notes list what you can bring to customers: what's **New**, **Competitive** points against named competitors, and **Licensing** changes, each with the words behind it, and **Relevant to** the customers whose meetings or account notes mention it. Files you add to **Training** give takeaways too, in its files summary. They come with the notes and summaries already written, with no extra AI requests. **Update All** lists the trainings of the last 90 days to add them to.
### Changed - **AI costs at a glance:** **Settings › AI › Usage** shows the last 7 days, with an optional **Weekly goal**; **Update All** shows about what the items you chose should cost, and says when they'd go past your goal. - **Lower AI costs:** notes, summaries, and briefs cite shorter quotes, at most three per statement, and **Update All** refreshes each opportunity's MEDDPICC once per run instead of once per meeting. - **Update All's count no longer stalls the window:** its checks of each customer's files and attachments are reused while nothing has changed, instead of read again every two minutes (on a library in Google Drive they could take seconds). - **Pre-call briefs are shorter and current:** a few lines per section, the newest first, leaving out what's settled. **New since last time** brings in what's new from trainings since your last meeting with the customer that fits it, such as a new feature or a point against their current vendor. **Since last time** is now **Last meeting**.

Internal and partner meetings about the customers they cover, each customer getting only what was said about it.
### Added - **Meetings about customers:** an internal or partner meeting, such as a pipeline review with your account executive, can be about one or more customers. Click **About** in the meeting's header, next to **Move To** (customers named in the meeting come first, also when they're called by their initials or a short name), or right-click meetings › **About Customer**. Each item of its notes then shows which customer it's about, or **Unclear**, with the words that tie it to that customer a click away; an item that names one of the customers goes to that one. Each customer's account summary, pre-call brief, and Ask AI get only what was said about it, as your team's view rather than the customer's. Right-click an item › **About** to correct it. A customer's meeting list shows these meetings under **Also about**. A meeting moved to **Internal** or **Partners** from a customer folder is marked once its notes are regenerated for its new folder.
### Changed - **The File menu:** **Send Folders to iPhone…** comes first, with **Import Meetings…** and **Export All Meetings…** together below it.

**Fieldbook 2.2.2 beta 2** (a beta)
The second beta of 2.2.2, on the beta channel: Macs set to **Beta** (Settings › General › Updates › Versions) get it as an automatic update. Everyone else stays on 2.2.1.
### Fixed - **Items marked Unclear when a customer goes by a short name:** in a meeting about a customer whose folder is, say, "Quillon W. Brask" but who's called "QW" on the call, every item was marked Unclear. With one customer on the meeting, the AI's choice now stands as long as its quote is real; with several, initials ("QW"), word starts run together ("WestMar" for Westbrook Marine), and a distinctive word of the name ("Brask") count as naming the customer, also in **About**'s "Mentioned in This Meeting". Items already marked are checked again on your Mac when Fieldbook starts, with no AI request. - **The About menu's "Mentioned in This Meeting"** could show the customers named in the meeting you looked at before, after moving a meeting from a customer folder to Internal or Partners. It now counts the meeting shown, again after a move. - **A meeting just moved to Internal or Partners** no longer has its items marked with customers twice: when its notes were written before the move, marking waits until they're regenerated for the new folder, and the notes say so.

Transcription that keeps going while you record, a step-by-step setup, and AI notes that follow your role.
### Added - **Set Up Fieldbook:** a step-by-step setup, one screen at a time: permissions, then the optional ones (Calendar, Reminders, Downloads, an email folder, Open at Login) with what each is for, AI notes, your name, role, and company, where meetings are saved (with a note on Google Drive or OneDrive for a cloud backup), and Release or Beta. It opens once after updating, filled in with your current settings; after that, from **Help › Set Up Fieldbook…** or **Settings › General**. It replaces the Welcome window on a new install.
### Changed - **Transcription keeps going while you record:** earlier meetings are transcribed, one at a time, during your next call, so their notes are ready sooner. **Settings › Transcription › Pause transcription while recording** (off) brings back the old wait, for a Mac that struggles during calls. - **Faster transcription:** part of the speech model now runs on the Neural Engine, about 10% faster, with slightly fewer words missed. The first transcription after updating takes a few extra seconds to prepare it. - **The Brief and the Detailed Summary:** the Brief is three to five takeaways for your team (what was decided, where things stand, what's next), even for a long meeting; the Detailed Summary is a full account of what was discussed, in order, with the names, numbers, and dates, sized to the meeting (about one item per two minutes, at most 25). - **AI that follows Your role:** with **Settings › General › Opportunities › Your role** set to Account Executive, the AI notes, account summary, pre-call brief, and next steps focus on budget, pricing, procurement, timeline, and who decides; as a Sales Engineer, on the customer's environment and requirements, as before. A recommended stage is suggested only for a Zscaler SE. - **Next steps for Salesforce:** **Write** now starts with an update line in your format, the date, your initials, and what happened ("10-14-26 - AJ - Met with customer, …"), then the open steps. **Copy** copies both. - **MEDDPICC from what the customer says:** your own questions and guesses in a meeting no longer count as evidence. - **Microsoft, not Microsoft Security:** the company you sell for, in **Settings › AI › Company** and **Set Up Fieldbook**, offers **Zscaler** and **Microsoft**. If you chose Microsoft Security, it's now Microsoft, with your solutions list as you left it. - **Diagnostic reports show power and heat:** the activity log in **Help › Save Diagnostic Report…** says whether the Mac was on battery or the power adapter, the battery level, Low Power Mode, and how hot it was running, at the start and end of each recording, while transcription runs during one, and whenever these change. It also says how long the speech model took to get ready.
### Fixed - **A microphone switch during a call** could, rarely, leave the Recorder showing the microphone as interrupted after it came back, and the saved meeting warning that its audio was missing until the end. - **A light line around the sidebar on macOS 26:** the sidebar now reaches the window's edges, as on macOS 15 and 27, so its outline no longer shows on the style's color. - **The sidebar's bottom rows:** with a long customer list, **Opportunities**, **Licensing**, and **My To-dos** drew over the last customers. They now sit below the list, which scrolls above them.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything in the six betas of 2.1.2, which ships to everyone as 2.2.
### Added
- **Opportunities for each customer:** a new **Opportunities** row under **Account** keeps each deal you track in Salesforce or your CRM, stacked one per line like a folder's emails: click one to open it with its close quarter (such as **Q2 FY27**), **Technical Validation Stage**, Open/Won/Lost, a link that opens it in your browser, and your notes, with **Copy** on every section to paste into the CRM. **New Opportunity…** starts one in this quarter. **New Opportunity…** asks only for the name and close quarter; add the stage, link, and the rest on its page. - **The recommended stage and MEDDPICC per opportunity,** from the meetings that count toward it, its notes and your account notes, and the customer's emails. Each customer meeting has an **Opportunity** menu next to its Brief (where the stage menu was); while a customer has one open opportunity, its meetings count toward it on their own. - **Next steps:** **Write** suggests an opportunity's open next steps from the briefs and to-dos of its meetings (crossed-off to-dos count as done) and its notes, each linked to the lines behind it. - **Suggested opportunities** from the opportunities in your meetings' AI notes: **Add…** starts one with its name, and the meetings it came up in count toward it. - **Opportunities, every customer's at once:** **Opportunities** at the bottom of the sidebar, above **Licensing**, is a quick view of all your opportunities in one table, grouped by the quarter they close in: customer, opportunity, stage, status, close date, and amount, with each quarter's **pipeline** (its open opportunities' amounts; won ones have their own total). Click an opportunity's name to open it on its customer's page, or a quarter on the left to go to it. **Show won and lost** and **Copy as Table** (for a spreadsheet). - **Amount, close date, and forecast type on each opportunity:** an **Amount** in dollars (type 240000, $240k, or 1.2m), a **Close date** (it sets the close quarter), and **New** or **Upsell**. All optional, on the opportunity's page; amounts show on its line. They stay on this Mac: none of them is sent to the AI. - **Settings › General › Opportunities › Fiscal year starts in** (August unless you change it), for close quarters. - **Your role, SE or AE:** **Settings › General › Opportunities › Your role**, Sales Engineer (the default) or Account Executive. Selling Zscaler, an AE's opportunities show Salesforce's **Opportunity Stage** (0 - Pipeline Generation to 5D - Approved, awaiting processing) instead of the Technical Validation Stage, on each opportunity and on the Opportunities page; **6 - Closed Won** and **7 - Closed Lost** mark it won or lost, and marking it won or lost sets them. The recommended stage is for SEs. An SE's stage and an AE's are kept apart, so changing roles loses neither. - **Your own stages and an Opp ID for other companies:** with Microsoft Security or your own company in Settings › AI, an opportunity's stage is a text field you fill in, and an **Opp ID** field sits under its link (kept on your Mac, never sent to the AI). - **A licensing library:** **Licensing**, at the bottom of the sidebar above **My To-dos**, keeps your own SKU sheets, feature matrices, price lists, licensing guides, and vendors' licensing web pages, and answers questions about them, such as which edition includes a feature or what else is needed above 5,000 users. Each point links to the row or page behind it (**L1**, **L2**, …): click to see the row with its columns, then **Open File** or **Copy Row**. Nothing is built in: each SE adds what they use, once, and the library stays through updates. - **Add File…** takes Excel, CSV, Word, PowerPoint, PDF, or text, with the company it's about (sources are grouped by company). Spreadsheets are read one row at a time with their column names, up to 20,000 rows a sheet. **Replace…** brings in a newer version. - **Add Link…** reads a web page, or the page and the pages under it (up to 200), from this Mac when you add it, and keeps a dated copy; **Refresh** reads it again. Fieldbook reads links only when you add or refresh them, over HTTPS, and respects the site's robots.txt. A PDF that's a copy of a page with the same name isn't read again, and if a site has more, the source says how many links were left unread. - **Ask AI uses the licensing library too:** a question in the toolbar's search field about licensing (a license, edition, SKU, tier, add-on, pricing, or what something includes) also gets the best matching rows and pages of your licensing sources, cited as **L1**, **L2**, … beside the meeting lines. - **Share the library:** the **⋯** menu in the Licensing list has **Share Library…**, one file with every source, and **Import Library…** for one a colleague shared (or drop it on the list). Their sources join yours; ones you already have are updated only by a newer copy. - **Licensing in AI notes:** when you have licensing sources, a meeting's opportunities are matched to them after its notes are written: under each opportunity, the SKUs, editions, or add-ons that fit and what else they need, linked to the rows behind them. **Match Licensing** (or **Match Again** after your sources change) does it on request. - **A Zscaler SKU spreadsheet on request:** with **Zscaler** as your company (Settings › AI), the Licensing page says how to get a sanitized, pre-built SKU and features spreadsheet to add: email ajaw@zscaler.com (the address opens a new email). - **Set the side when you mark someone:** the **Who's talking?** box has a menu beside the name: **Internal**, **Customer**, **Partner**, or **Other**, also **Command-1** to **Command-4** while you type. It shows the side of the person you've chosen (an invitee or someone you've met) and starts as **Side** (not set) for a name you type; after the call, **Yes** gives the speaker that side. Clicking a mark in the meeting's header opens the box with its name filled in, so you can change just the side. - **Yes on a speaker mark sets the side too:** for a name you typed when marking, **Yes ⌄** under **Speakers** offers **Internal**, **Customer**, **Partner**, or **Other**, so one choice names the speaker and sets their side, without opening the speaker afterwards. A mark that knows the side (an invitee or someone you've met) shows it, as "Priya Shah (Customer)?", with a plain **Yes**. - **Remove a speaker mark made by mistake:** while recording, each mark in the meeting's header has a **✕**; after the call, so does its ⚑ line in the transcript, and the mark's row under **Speakers** has **Remove** next to Yes and No. Right-clicking a mark offers **Remove Mark** too. - **Change a mark's name while recording:** click a mark in the meeting's header to open **Who's talking?** again and choose someone else (or **No Name**); **Escape** keeps it as it was. - **Links in your notes:** web and email addresses in your meeting notes, account notes, and opportunities' notes are links: click one to open it in your browser, or point at it to see where it goes. - **Import transcripts from Word:** **Import Transcript…** and dropping a file now take `.docx` transcripts, such as Teams' **Download as .docx** (newer files with "Name 0:03" before each turn, and older ones with "0:0:0.0 --> 0:0:5.1" timings), with their speakers and times. The meeting's title, date, and length at the top and Teams' "started transcription" lines are left out. A Word document without times still becomes a manual meeting with its text in your notes. (`.txt` transcripts, including Zoom's export, were already imported.) - **The meeting being recorded, in the sidebar:** while recording, the meeting shows at the bottom of the **Recorder**, just above **Library**. Click it to go back to its notes after looking at a customer, a label, another folder, My To-dos, or Licensing. - **Keep or trash the .zip from your iPhone:** after a recording AirDropped from Fieldbook for iPhone is imported, a small **Imported from Your iPhone** window lists what came in and asks whether to keep the .zip files in Downloads or move them to the Trash. Several imports share one window, and while you're recording it waits until you stop. **Always do this** stops the question; change it in **Settings › General › Downloads**. - **Folders to the iPhone by themselves:** **File › Send Folders to iPhone…** now marks the file as coming from this Mac, so Fieldbook for iPhone (build 15 and later), watching its Downloads, uses each new one without asking once you've used folders from this Mac. - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.2:** shown once after updating, with the two new places in the sidebar, **Opportunities** (with your fiscal year and **Show Opportunities**) and **Licensing** (**Open Licensing**), and what else is new since 2.1.
### Changed
- **Update All writes each account summary once:** while one of a customer's meetings is recording, being transcribed, or waiting for its automatic notes, its account summary is listed greyed out with what it's waiting for, instead of being written now and again when the notes arrive. An account summary that's up to date but would be changed by the meetings above it is listed as **Then, if the above change it**, so one run finishes the job instead of two. Update All's count leaves both out. - **Fewer AI requests after notes are written again:** the follow-up email is drafted automatically only with a meeting's first notes; afterwards your draft stays, marked as drafted before the notes changed, with **Redraft**. A meeting's licensing match is kept when its opportunities and your licensing sources haven't changed. - **The stage, MEDDPICC, and the recommended stage moved from meetings and the account to each opportunity.** The Account page starts with the customer's open opportunities, then account notes and the account summary. A customer whose meetings set a stage, or that had MEDDPICC, offers **Start an Opportunity with It…**, which brings both along. - **Update All** lists MEDDPICC per open opportunity, counting an opportunity's changes within a couple of seconds, and the pre-call brief uses the open opportunity's MEDDPICC. - **The account summary reads the customer's opportunities:** "Where things stand" names each open one with its close quarter and stage, using your notes on it; a statement that comes from an opportunity lists it among its sources. Adding or changing an opportunity (its stage, quarter, status, name, or notes) marks the summary out of date, so **Update** brings it up to date with just that opportunity, and removing one asks for a rewrite.
### Fixed
- **Update All's button counts again after a run finishes in the background:** closing its window while it works no longer leaves the button saying "Updated" until you open it and choose Done; once the run ends, the button shows what's still out of date. - **Rename Label and Rename Customer** show the name you're typing clearly: with a two-tone style it was light text on the box's white field.
